paper_title: RNA Inverse Folding Can Be Solved in Linear Time for Structures Without Isolated Stacks or Base Pairs
statement: obtained with (modulo)-separated colorings. More importantly, does the space of (modulo)- separated colorings always/often contain a design with respect to the nearest-neighborhood Turner energy model? Even if it unlikely to hold unconditionally, it is plausible that some extensions of separability and m-separability will achieve theoretical and practical solutions for inverse folding in more general energy models. As a first step, separability in a stacking energy model seems a relevant goal, even if less ambitious than the Turner model. It would probably require to go beyond the current coloring formalism, and motivate the introduction of more general notions of defect to capture imbalance at the dinucleotide level.
